set.n: Herman Lunning's hidden money, recluse's cabin in the hills north of Galena
set.pl: Cabin in the hills a few miles north of Galena, near the Illinois Central tracks; pin about 3.5 km NNW of Galena, cabin not yet placed
set.st: Jan 1916: Herman Lunning, a recluse of about 70 with no relatives, was found dying beside the Illinois Central tracks north of Galena on his way home to his cabin in the hills, a splinter driven into his skull. Stories said he had an enormous fortune hidden somewhere about his cabin; his pockets were not robbed, and it was thought his attackers were after the cache. Action was planned to have his premises searched. No find was reported.
set.t: Earlier wire copies said 'near Dubuque', but the Dubuque special and the Freeport paper put him in Illinois, north of Galena. Two separate papers, so C. The money was said to be hidden about the cabin, not on him. Find the cabin on a 1910s Jo Daviess plat (the 1925 plat may show the land under a later owner) or in the Galena Gazette for Jan 1916. Private land: ask permission.
src: Cedar Rapids Gazette 24 Jan 1916 p3, Dubuque special (Newspapers.com 547631199)
El Paso Herald 24 Jan 1916 (TN TreasureNet thread 615030)
pinev: Town-level: the 1916 accounts put the cabin in the hills a few miles north of Galena near the Illinois Central tracks (about 4 km).
set.tovw: Lead grade C: two separate papers (IA/IL thread)
